index.title: Axomis Labs — Thoughtful Solutions
index.description: Axomis Labs designs and engineers digital products, systems, and experiences that turn complexity into clarity — with people at the centre of every solution.
index.og_description: Digital products, systems, and experiences that turn complexity into clarity.
index.hero_lead: Axomis Labs designs and engineers digital products, systems, and experiences — built with care for the people who will actually use them.
index.work_h2: Four disciplines, one way of thinking.
index.work_intro: We don't define ourselves by a particular technology. Our work is defined by the quality of the thinking behind it — which is why we move comfortably between products, platforms, and consulting engagements.

work_cards.title: Software Engineering
work_cards.body: We architect and build systems that hold up over time — enterprise platforms, consumer applications, and the infrastructure beneath them. Engineering discipline, applied where it matters.

work_cards.title: Digital Product Design
work_cards.body: Interfaces and experiences shaped around real behaviour, so that using them feels natural rather than learned. Every interface shapes an experience; every decision influences trust.

work_cards.title: Consulting
work_cards.body: Clear thinking for organisations navigating change — including regulated industries, where the margin for error is small and the cost of ambiguity is high.

work_cards.title: Process & Systems
work_cards.body: We examine how work actually happens, then remove the friction nobody budgeted for. Processes should feel natural; complexity should become clarity.

index.philosophy_pull:
The best solutions rarely begin with code.
They begin with listening.

philosophy_steps.title: Listen
philosophy_steps.body: Before proposing anything, we understand the problem as the people living with it experience it.

philosophy_steps.title: Understand
philosophy_steps.body: We map the system around the problem — technical, organisational, and human.

philosophy_steps.title: Ask better questions
philosophy_steps.body: Only then do we choose the technologies, architectures, and tools that genuinely solve it.

index.philosophy_closing: Rather than chasing trends, we pursue solutions that remain valuable long after the newest technology has changed. The industries may change. The technologies will evolve. Our principles remain.

values.title: Thoughtfulness
values.body: Every decision deserves consideration. Good technology begins with understanding people.

values.title: Clarity
values.body: We reduce complexity. We create systems that people can trust and understand.

values.title: Craftsmanship
values.body: We value quality over speed. Details matter, because details shape experiences.

values.title: Curiosity
values.body: We continue learning. Innovation begins with asking better questions.

values.title: Integrity
values.body: We act transparently and responsibly. Trust is earned through consistency.

values.title: Human Experience
values.body: Technology should support people, not overwhelm them. Every interaction can make life simpler.

references.title: References — Axomis Labs
references.description: Selected work from Axomis Labs — experience, our own products, and consulting engagements.
references.og_description: Experience, our own products, and consulting engagements.
experience_prose: Behind Axomis Labs sits more than a decade of system and database architecture, implementation and project management in the pharmaceutical industry — an environment where a system isn't considered working until it has been proven to work, and where every change carries documentation and accountability.

Alongside that, years of computerised systems validation: making systems run seamlessly while satisfying every compliance constraint around them. It teaches a particular habit — designing for evidence, not only for function.

Less obviously, twenty-five years of sport across very different disciplines — combat sports, ball sports, volleyball, dance, diving. What carries into the work isn't the sport but the habit behind it: focus, discipline, and knowing what it takes to get good at something unfamiliar. It is also why the industry isn't the point — what transfers is the discipline, not the domain.

experience_tiles.title: Regulated systems
experience_tiles.body: 10+ years of architecture, implementation and project management in pharma, where correctness is a requirement rather than an aspiration.

experience_tiles.title: Validation & compliance
experience_tiles.body: Computerised systems validation — building systems that run seamlessly and can still be evidenced against the rules that govern them.

experience_tiles.title: Focus & discipline
experience_tiles.body: Twenty-five years of sport across unrelated disciplines. What transfers is the focus, and the discipline to stay with something until it is genuinely good.

references.experience_note: The approach isn't tied to one sector. It transfers wherever systems have to be made to work and stand up to scrutiny — pharmaceutical and other regulated environments included.
references.products_h2: Software we build and run ourselves.
references.products_intro: Carrying our own products through design, release and support.

products.title: TournaQ Volley
products.body: A games and tournament management platform, built to support the processes that happen on the field. Designed to bring people together, and to let organisers and players run events smoothly — without the friction that usually comes with them.

products.title: DoQLoom
products.body: Reads documents, extracts the data that matters, and files them automatically into a structured hierarchy that can be analysed later. Integrates with Google Drive and conforms with GDPR, so you can focus on the filing process rather than on where the data ends up.

products.title: Workout planning

products.title: More in the pipeline

references.consulting_h2: Work that starts before the software does.
references.consulting_intro: From a single application to a company-wide step up in digitalisation — and the online presence that goes with it. Scoped to whatever the business actually needs next.

consulting_tiles.title: Project & organisation management
consulting_tiles.body: Structuring work so it can be planned, delegated and finished — with decisions prepared, documented and open to review later.

consulting_tiles.title: Data & process management
consulting_tiles.body: Getting data into one dependable place and the processes around it into a shape that holds — contract capture, document filing, payments and scheduling included, from industrial operations through to sports applications.

consulting_tiles.title: Product management
consulting_tiles.body: Deciding what to build, in what order, and what to leave out — then staying with it through delivery rather than handing over a specification.

consulting_tiles.title: Implementation
consulting_tiles.body: Taking a system from requirements engineering through testing to the production handshake, and staying with it until it runs. Shaped by regulated work, where nothing goes live without the evidence to support it.

consulting_tiles.title: Software selection
consulting_tiles.body: Comparing what's on the market against what you need, so you buy the right thing — or find out early that building is the better answer.

consulting_tiles.title: Digital transformation
consulting_tiles.body: For smaller companies wanting to move faster: one central archive instead of scattered folders, contracts captured automatically instead of by hand, and key figures that are simply there — going as far as reworking revenue streams through digitalisation.

consulting_tiles.title: Web presence
consulting_tiles.body: The site itself and everything that keeps it running. Static pages or WordPress — decided by who maintains it afterwards rather than by what is quickest to build — and carrying the same message as everything else you publish.

consulting_tiles.title: Social media campaigns
consulting_tiles.body: Strategy, plan and production for a specific occasion: a new location, an extension, a launch. Planned as a sequence with an arc rather than post by post.

references.consulting_note: Engagements are shaped to fit — a defined project, ongoing support, or a bespoke arrangement where that suits both sides better.

references/social-media-campaigns.title: Social media campaigns — Axomis Labs
references/social-media-campaigns.description: Strategy, campaign plan and production for a specific occasion — planned as a sequence with an arc and built as a system you can keep running.
references/social-media-campaigns.og_description: Assessment, positioning, release plan and production — with a worked example.
references/social-media-campaigns.hero_lead: A campaign exists to do something: bring in members, customers or bookings, and put distance between you and whoever else is competing for the same attention. We start by working out what you genuinely have that the others cannot claim — then plan a sequence that carries it over weeks instead of spending it in one post.

method.title: Assessment
method.body: What is already there and what is actually happening: your channel and its reach, who follows it, what the competition is doing, and what the occasion is. Nothing is produced before this is written down.

method.title: Your own strengths
method.body: What you have that the others cannot claim. It is usually more concrete than a slogan — a room, a piece of equipment, a range of classes, a location. That becomes the line the whole campaign is built on.

method.title: Release plan
method.body: A fixed schedule across the weeks around the occasion: what is announced when, where the teasers sit, where the reveal sits. The arc is the point — it holds attention over time rather than spending it at once, and it gives followers a reason to keep watching.

method.title: Production and handover
method.body: Everything the plan calls for, built from one design system, plus the files and instructions to carry on afterwards.

references/social-media-campaigns.package_intro: The assessment ends in a plan. The plan names all of this, and the scope is agreed before anything is produced.

package.title: Positioning and message
package.body: The one line the campaign is built on, and the reasoning behind it.

package.title: Editorial plan
package.body: Feed, stories and reels laid out across the weeks, each item briefed well enough that someone else could produce it.

package.title: Art direction
package.body: How it looks and why — decided once, against the message, not per post.

package.title: Design system and templates
package.body: Format, colour, typeface, logo and margins fixed centrally, so the series reads as a series and new posts stay consistent.

package.title: Production and copy
package.body: The assets themselves, the text that goes with them, image work and compositing from the material that already exists.

package.title: Handover and documentation
package.body: Source files and plain-language instructions, so the system keeps working without us.

case_prose: A martial arts school in Bielefeld is adding a second hall: over 850 m² across two floors, striking upstairs and ground work downstairs. That is a real improvement in what members get, and it opens in November.

It is also not the only news in town — a competitor in the same city has built as well and is posting about it. So the task was not to announce an opening. It was to make the difference legible, carry it across four weeks of posts, stories and reels, and turn it into trial sessions and sign-ups rather than one good day of reach.

The assessment produced the line the campaign is built on: two levels, two disciplines, one school — something the competitor cannot claim. Everything after that was produced against it: the release plan, the design system, the templates and the review page below. The campaign runs from the opening, and measurement runs with it from the first day.
references/social-media-campaigns.case_note: What the finished work looks like — the review page the client signs off on:
references/social-media-campaigns.models_h2: Run by us, or by you.
models_prose: Once the system exists, someone has to operate it. That can be us — planning, producing and publishing on the agreed schedule — or your own team, working from the templates and the plan. Most engagements land in between: we carry the launch phase, you take over once it is running.
Which way round it goes is decided when the plan is written, not before. Anything beyond that we work out in a conversation.
